content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper provides a LSTM model with joint spatiotemporal attention for mortality prediction of long covid patients, which considers the weight for both time and clinical features. Furthermore, authors consider the local LSTM for separate learning of short and long-term dependency. The experiment shows AUC improvement in mortality prediction from the normal LSTM model and clinical model. In addition, the authors provide a key prognostic biomarker for severe long COVID based on the correlation of different time points.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
1. The paper provides a novel idea considering attention for both time features and clinical features when building RNN Model. 
2. Significantly AUC improvement of the purposed method compared with regular LSTM. 
3. Clear data dataset explanation and the consideration of mutiple data sources, such as medical images and medical history. 

Weakness: 
1. Since the proposed method is a medical prediction model, it is important to provide a solid either clinically meaningful explanation of the model, or a clinical explanation of the result, especially the part of identifying key prognostic biomarkers. However, both detailed work are not shown in this paper. 
2. More metrics are needed for the prediction experiment rather than only AUC. 
3. Similar idea of considering both time and clinical features are already been considered by recently published papers. Therefore, at least comparing with these method are necessary. (eg. Yang, F. et al. DeepMPM: a mortality risk prediction model using longitudinal EHR data. BMC Bioinformatics 23, 423 (2022). )
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: 
Most of the parts in the paper are quite good. However, it could be better to show more detail about these things. 
1. The graph you showed in Local-LSTM does not have the number of layers. Is that mean you use one layer model in this part? 
2. You only mention significantly (p ≤ 0.05) correlated critical time points between joint spatiotemporal attention and Apache II system. At least the correation matrix graph should be shown to illustrate this point. Further statistical analysis is also necessary to identify the key time point. 
3. Does your model require the same time points for each subject? Please specify.  

The overall quality is good. And the novelty needs concerns since similar idea has been published recently as mentioned in the weakness part.  In addition, point 1 and 2 in clarity part will affect people to reproduce the method.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the paper provides an idea considering attention for both time features and clinical features when building LSTM Model and gives detailed experiments on real data and observed improvement on AUC. However,  similar idea has been published recently as mentioned in the weakness part. In addition, it is important to provide a solid either clinically meaningful explanation of the model, or a clinical interpretation of the result for a medical prediction model. Several clarity issues should also be solved mentioned in the clarity part.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed the use of a spatiotemporal attention model for mortality prediction of Long Covid. It argues to capture the importance of learning the feature importance at different time points using a spatiotemporal attention and to use local-LSTM to feature local features for handling the local randomness in the patient records. A Long Covid dataset with 396 patients were used for the validation to show that adopting the two proposed tricks can enhance the mortality prediction accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ The problem is interesting.
+ The proposed tricks are reasonable.

Weaknesses:
- The two proposed tricks include the use of local LSTMs and a particular spatiotemporal attention architecture, where the technical contribution is limited. Also, it is unclear if this is only applicable for this particular case, or it can be generalized for other applications. If it can be generalized for other applications, there should be other methodologies proposed with a similar goal to be achieved. Given what being carried out and presented in the paper, the study is a bit preliminary at this stage.
- The size of the dataset of Long COVID is small. It is understandable that it may not be easy to have too many Long COVID patient record. But that makes the potential impact of the paper unclear.
- Presentation can be further improved. i) The introduction covers a general overview of related analytics works based on covid data of different modalities (from structured records to X-ray image). Making it focusing more on the problem setting adopted in the paper seems to be better. ii) The motivation behind the design of the proposed solutions can be further elaborated.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As explained in the "Strengths and Weaknesses" section, the technical novelty is limited. The clarity and quality are also fair. Please refer to the "Strengths and Weaknesses" section.
content.summary_of_the_review: The problem being studied is interested where understanding the long covid effect on patient is important. While the technical tricks proposed are reasonable, the underlying technical novelty is limited. The validation was carried out using a relatively small dataset. The potential impact of the results presented in the paper is also limited. The paper is readable but the overall organization should be improved as suggested.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a spatiotemporal attention model for predicting mortality of patients with long Covid. The authors show that the proposed model outperforms various baselines on a hard-to-acquire long Covid dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The long Covid problem that the paper addresses is important
2. The proposed method is straightforward to understand
3. The dataset analyzed appears to be quite interesting (and I appreciate the effort that has gone into acquiring this dataset)

Weaknesses:
1. My main concern is that the proposed method simply does not seem that novel. For instance, Rosnati and Fortuin [2021] have proposed a model called MGP-AttTCN that, while different in some aspects, is conceptually very similar in many ways and also uses an attention mechanism. See also the attention-based model called RETAIN that is by Choi et al [2016]. Explaining how the proposed method compares with these existing methods and also benchmarking against them in experiments would better give a sense of how the proposed method compares to the state-of-the-art.
2. There are no error bars reported in Tables 1 and 2. I would suggest figuring out a way to set up the experiment so that we get a better sense of uncertainty in prediction results. For example, you could re-run training with 10 different random seeds and report mean/std dev across random seeds.

References:
- Edward Choi, Mohammad Taha Bahadori, Jimeng Sun, Joshua Kulas, Andy Schuetz, Walter Stewart. RETAIN: An Interpretable Predictive Model for Healthcare using Reverse Time Attention Mechanism. NeurIPS 2016.
- Margherita Rosnati, Vincent Fortuin. MGP-AttTCN: An interpretable machine learning model for the prediction of sepsis. PLOS One 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
**Clarity.** The paper is reasonably clear.

**Quality/novelty.** My main concern is that the proposed method is actually not that novel. The authors have not appropriately compared with relevant existing methods (see the first weakness point that I stated above). Consequently it is unclear why one should favor using this new model when there is already at least one existing model that is quite similar.

**Reproducibility.** From what I can tell, neither the data nor the code is available so reproducing the results would be challenging. Perhaps adding experimental results on an additional dataset that is publicly available (e.g., some subset of MIMIC or eICU) would be helpful here so that other researchers could at least attempt to reproduce results on this publicly available dataset.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, while I found this paper interesting to read, the problem addressed to be very important, the proposed method to be promising, and the dataset used to be quite interesting, my major concern is in the limited novelty of the proposed method, especially in comparison to existing attention-based methods (such as MGP-AttTCN and RETAIN), which were not discussed nor compared against in experiments.

content.title: Joint Spatiotemporal Attention for Mortality Prediction of Patients with Long COVID
content.TL;DR: We proposed a joint spatiotemporal attention mechanism for deep learning-based mortality prediction of long covid.
content.abstract: Long COVID is a general term of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19. Patients with Long COVID can endure long-lasting symptoms including fatigue, headache, dyspnea and anosmia, facing increased risk of death. Identifying the cohorts with severe long-term complications in COVID-19 could benefit the treatment planning and resource arrangement. However, due to the heterogeneous phenotypes and various duration of symptoms presented in patients with Long COVID, it is difficult to predict their outcomes from their longitudinal data. In this study, we proposed a spatiotemporal attention mechanism to weigh feature importance jointly from the temporal dimension and feature space of longitudinal medical data. Considering that medical examinations can have interchangeable orders in adjacent time points, we restricted the learning of short-term dependency with a Local-LSTM and the learning of long-term dependency with the joint spatiotemporal attention. We also compared the proposed method with several state-of-the-art methods and a method in clinical practice. The methods are evaluated on a hard-to-acquire clinical dataset of patients with Long COVID. Experimental results show the Local-LSTM with joint spatiotemporal attention achieved superior performance in mortality prediction comparing to related methods. By analyzing the critical time points identified by the joint spatiotemporal attention, we identified time-specific prognostic biomarkers for life-threatening Long COVID. The proposed method provides a clinical tool for the severity assessment of Long COVID.
